thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1: KV cache OOMs detected on hosted-runtime-prod. Multiple runtime pods in shard-group-A hit OOM at 00:43 UTC. Evictions failing, continuous-batching map growth skyrocketing. Paging @sre-oncall.

sre-oncall: ACK. Jumping in, joining bridge. Collecting logs + current metrics. Assigning triage owner: marta.

marta: seen it — 5 OOMs in last 2m on runtime-03/04/07. KV map growth from ~1GB -> 9.2GB in ~90s. Eviction attempts logged but memory still climbs.

akash: this looks like runaway context windows / long prompts triggering continuous-batching to keep large KV caches. Quick mitigation: reduce continuous_batching.max_window and throttle prefetch. We did something similar before.

luca: agree. Suggest immediate mitigations: 1) disable prefetch for hosted tier, 2) set continuous_batching.max_window=1024, 3) force eviction policy to aggressive-LRU. We can patch via runtime-config service.

marta: logs (excerpt):
```
2026-03-15T00:42:58Z runtime-03 ERROR kv_cache: map_size=9223372036 entries=482312 evict_attempt=1
2026-03-15T00:43:01Z runtime-03 WARN continuous_batching: ctx_span=87345 tokens=120k prefetch=on
2026-03-15T00:43:02Z runtime-07 CRIT oom-kernel: process killed due to OOM
```

sre-oncall: OK applying patch now. Patching hosted-runtime config to cap window and disable prefetch for route /generate.

akash: example patch we can apply quickly:
```
continuous_batching:
  max_window: 1024
  kv_prefetch: false
batching:
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
```
Will roll as a fastfollow canary to 10% traffic.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: started rollout for runtime-config/hosted-patch-517263 on 10% canary.

marta: running smoke checks against canary.

sre-oncall: canary looks healthy at 10m. No OOMs on canary nodes. Rolling to 50% now.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: canary -> 50% rollout success.

luca: still seeing high memory on older nodes, triggering forced evictions. I'll trigger eviction script on shard-group-A: `./scripts/evict-heavy-sessions --shard A --threshold 2GB`.

sre-oncall: eviction script run -> freed ~6.2GB on runtime-03, runtime-04. Memory pressure dropping.

jamie: customer impact check: error rate for text-generation (hosted) spiked to 3.4% in last 10m. Latency also up for long-context sessions. Top source appears to be a single large customer (synapse.ai) with sessions >50k tokens.

cs-led: I'll open a priority support thread and start customer outreach. Drafting message: "We're seeing elevated memory usage causing transient failures on long-context sessions. We're applying mitigations and will follow up with details." Want approval before sending.

marta: fine to send provisional note, include severity and ask them to migrate large session workloads to dedicated for now if they need high-context spans. cs-led please cc account team.

akash: follow-up: we should throttle prefetch rate as an additional belt: set prefetch_rate_limit=10 req/s for hosted-prod. Also add server-side session span cap (hard cap at 128k tokens) with soft rejection responses for apps.

luca: leaving a quick config snippet to apply after immediate hotfix:
```
prefetch:
  enabled: true
  rate_limit: 10
session:
  hard_span_cap_tokens: 131072
  soft_span_warning_tokens: 65536
```

sre-oncall: scaling action: temporarily adding +4 nodes to hosted-runtime pool to absorb user traffic while we stabilize. Started scale-up via infra autoscale endpoint.

incident-bot: infra-bot: scale up request accepted, provisioning 4 nodes (expected ready 6m).

marta: metrics are improving post-patch+evict: KV map growth rate flattened, no new OOMs on patched nodes. Will keep patch in place for 1hr and monitor.

jamie: CS confirms synapse.ai experiencing errors but not data loss. They're requesting ETA for a permanent fix; flagged for product/eng follow-up.

akash: action items (short):
- make batch_config hotfix permanent if passes 4h window
- add alert: kv_map_growth > 4GB in 5m -> P1
- add session span caps and server-side soft rejections
- consider route-based prefetch disable for hosted

luca: ops checklist added to incident doc. Also planning a postmortem to cover: root cause (long prompts + continuous batching retention), regression vector (recent batch-window change from last week), and mitigation plan (prefetch throttles + session caps).

cs-led: sent customer update to synapse.ai. They acknowledged and agreed to throttle client-side for now.

sre-oncall: summary: mitigation applied (continuous_batching.max_window=1024, kv_prefetch disabled for /generate, forced evictions run, +4 nodes scaled), customer notified, metrics improving. Keeping P1 for now. Next update in 30m or sooner if anything changes. Handoff to marta for monitoring.

marta: handing off active monitoring to day-shift. If any new OOMs appear or KV growth restarts, escalate to eng-runtime and page oncall-senior.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident record created: https://redwood.internal/incident/517263

sre-oncall: leaving bridge. Good job team.
